questions.question: After the 97th Constitutional Amendment, for how long can a state co-operative law that is inconsistent with the amendment remain in force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 97th Constitutional Amendment introduced reforms to promote the autonomy and democratic functioning of cooperative societies in India.
 
• Under this amendment, state laws inconsistent with the provisions of the amendment can remain in force for a maximum period of **1 year** from the commencement of the amendment.
 
• This period allows states to make necessary modifications to their cooperative laws to comply with the amendment.
 
• The amendment aimed to make cooperative societies more accountable, transparent, and member-driven.
 
• It also added a new part, Part IXB, to the Constitution of India to specifically deal with cooperative societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **97th Constitutional Amendment:**

 
 
• The amendment was passed in 2011 and came into effect on February 15, 2012.
 
• It added Article 43B to the Directive Principles of State Policy, encouraging states to promote voluntary formation, democratic functioning, and professional management of cooperative societies.
 
 
 
• **Part IXB of the Constitution:**
 
 
• This part specifically deals with cooperative societies and outlines provisions for their governance.
 
• It includes provisions for the composition, election, and tenure of the board of cooperative societies.
 
 
 
• **Objective of the Amendment:**
 
 
• To improve the functioning of cooperative societies and ensure their accountability to members.
 
• To protect the interests of members and prevent misuse of funds and powers.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework:**
 
 
• States were required to amend their cooperative society laws to comply with the constitutional provisions within one year.
 
• Any inconsistent state law beyond this period would cease to have effect.

questions.question: The term 'Bhukti' in post-Gupta polity referred to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Province**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'Bhukti'** in post-Gupta period referred to an administrative division or a **province**.
 
• Bhuktis were governed by officers known as **'Uparikas'**, who were appointed by the king.
 
• Each Bhukti consisted of multiple **'Vishayas'** or districts, which were smaller administrative units.
 
• The Vishayas were managed by officers called **'Vishayapatis'**, who reported to the Uparikas of the Bhukti.
 
• Bhuktis were a key feature of the decentralized administrative structure during the post-Gupta era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Uparika:** The head of a Bhukti, appointed by the king, who held administrative and judicial authority over the province.
 
• **Vishaya:** A sub-division of a Bhukti, equivalent to a district, managed by Vishayapatis.
 
• **Post-Gupta Polity:** This period saw a shift towards a more decentralized administrative system, with provinces playing a critical role in governance.
 
• **Decentralization:** The post-Gupta administration was characterized by a division of power between central and provincial authorities.
 
• **Gupta Administration:** The Gupta era laid the foundation for administrative units like Bhuktis and Vishayas, which continued in post-Gupta polity.

questions.question: Who authored the book 'Hind Swaraj', which outlined the principles of non-violent resistance and self-rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Hind Swaraj'** was written by Mahatma Gandhi in **1909** during his voyage from **England to South Africa**.
 
• The book outlines Gandhi's **philosophy of non-violent resistance** (Satyagraha) and his vision of self-rule (Swaraj) for India.
 
• It critiques Western civilization and industrialization, advocating for a return to **simple, self-sufficient village life**.
 
• The book serves as a foundational text for the Indian independence movement and reflects Gandhi's belief in **truth, non-violence, and self-reliance**.
 
• 'Hind Swaraj' has been translated into several languages and remains a key text in understanding **Gandhian philosophy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satyagraha:**

 
 
• A key concept in Gandhi's philosophy, it means **"insistence on truth"** or non-violent resistance.
 
• It was employed in various movements such as the **Champaran Satyagraha** and the **Dandi March**.
 
• Satyagraha emphasizes moral strength over physical force to achieve justice and freedom.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj:**
 
 
• Literally translates to **"self-rule"** or "**self-governance**."
 
• In 'Hind Swaraj,' Gandhi advocated for Swaraj not just as political independence but also as **individual and community self-reliance**.
 
• It involves decentralization of power and promotion of local industries and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Critique of Western Civilization:**
 
 
• In 'Hind Swaraj,' Gandhi criticizes the materialism and industrialization of Western societies.
 
• He attributes the erosion of moral and spiritual values to the **overemphasis on machinery and technology**.
 
• Instead, he advocates for a lifestyle rooted in simplicity, spirituality, and community well-being.

questions.question: What will happen when a plant cell is put in a medium having higher water concentration than the cell?

options.text: It will not show any change

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**It will likely swell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **plant cell** is placed in a medium with higher water concentration (hypotonic solution) than the cell, water enters the cell due to **osmosis**.
 
• **Osmosis** is the movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a **semi-permeable membrane**.
 
• Plant cells have a **rigid cell wall** that prevents them from bursting under osmotic pressure.
 
• The entry of water into the cell causes the **vacuole** to expand, pushing the cell membrane against the cell wall, leading to the cell swelling.
 
• The pressure exerted by the swollen vacuole against the cell wall is called **turgor pressure**, which helps maintain the shape and rigidity of the cell.
 
• This swelling is critical for the plant's **structural integrity and physiological processes**, such as nutrient transport and photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It will not show any change**__

 __
 
• This would occur if the plant cell was placed in an **isotonic solution**, where the concentration of water is the same inside and outside the cell.
 
• No net movement of water occurs, and the cell remains unchanged.
 
 
 
• **It will likely shrink**__
 __
 
• This happens when the plant cell is placed in a **hypertonic solution**, where the water concentration outside the cell is lower than inside.
 
• Water moves out of the cell, causing the cell to lose turgor pressure and shrink, a process known as **plasmolysis**.
 
 
 
• **It will burst**__
 
 
• Plant cells do not burst due to the presence of a **rigid cell wall**, which can withstand high internal pressure.
 
• This option is applicable to **animal cells**, which lack a cell wall and may burst in a hypotonic solution.

questions.question: The Shakas were defeated by which tribal group before entering India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Yueh-chis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Yueh-chis were a nomadic tribe originally from the region of modern-day Central Asia (near the Tarim Basin).
 
• They defeated the Shakas (Scythians) before entering India and displaced them from their original territories.
 
• After their victory over the Shakas, the Yueh-chis migrated southward and established their dominance in regions near present-day Afghanistan and Pakistan.
 
• The Yueh-chis later formed the Kushan Empire under their leader Kujula Kadphises, significantly influencing Indian history and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shakas (Scythians):**

 
 
• The Shakas were a nomadic Indo-European group originating from Central Asia.
 
• They are known for migrating into India and establishing kingdoms like the Western Kshatrapas.
 
• The Shakas contributed to cultural exchanges between Central Asia and India, including art and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Yueh-chis:**
 
 
• The Yueh-chis were displaced by the Xiongnu from their original homeland in Central Asia.
 
• They migrated south and played a pivotal role in shaping the cultural and political landscape of ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Kushan Empire:**
 
 
• The Kushan Empire was founded by the Yueh-chis and reached its zenith under Emperor Kanishka.
 
• It promoted Buddhism and played a crucial role in connecting the Silk Road trade network.
 
 
 
• **Silk Road Connection:**
 
 
• The migration of nomadic tribes like the Yueh-chis contributed to the establishment of trade routes connecting India, Central Asia, and China.
 
• The exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures along the Silk Road significantly influenced Indian history.

questions.question: Which schedule allows for the creation of village councils or courts for tribal cases?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixth Schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Sixth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution provides for the **administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• It allows for the establishment of **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs)**, which are empowered to make laws and govern certain aspects of administration in tribal areas.
 
• The ADCs are authorized to create **village councils or courts** for handling disputes and cases involving tribal individuals, ensuring their customary laws and practices are preserved.
 
• This schedule provides a legal framework to protect the rights and culture of tribal communities while granting them **self-governance**.
 
• The Sixth Schedule seeks to empower tribal regions by granting them autonomy in areas such as land use, resource management, and administration of justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Autonomous District Councils (ADCs):**

 
 
• ADCs are created under the Sixth Schedule to administer tribal areas and protect tribal rights.
 
• They have the authority to legislate on matters such as land, forests, water, customs, and inheritance.
 
• ADCs are composed of members both elected and nominated by the Governor of the respective state.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Courts:**
 
 
• Village councils or courts established under ADCs are empowered to handle cases involving tribal individuals in accordance with customary laws.
 
• These courts aim to ensure quick and culturally sensitive resolution of disputes within tribal communities.
 
 
 
• **Other Schedules Related to Tribals:**
 
 
• The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in other states (excluding the Sixth Schedule states).
 
• The Sixth Schedule, however, provides a more autonomous framework for certain northeastern states.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Sixth Schedule:**
 
 
• It preserves the unique cultural identity and traditions of tribal communities.
 
• It ensures self-governance and participatory democracy within tribal areas.

questions.question:
Identify the balanced chemical equation for the following reaction. 

Mg + O₂ → MgO
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg + 1/2 O₂ → MgO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The balanced chemical equation for the formation of magnesium oxide (MgO) from magnesium (Mg) and oxygen (O₂) is: **2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO**.
 
• To balance the chemical equation, ensure that the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides of the equation.
 
• In this reaction, 2 moles of magnesium react with 1 mole of oxygen gas to produce 2 moles of magnesium oxide.
 
• The balanced equation reflects the conservation of mass, where the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products.
 
• Magnesium oxide is a white solid that forms when magnesium metal burns in the presence of oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:**

 
 
• This fundamental principle states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• In a balanced chemical equation, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
 
 
 
• **Balancing Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• The process of balancing chemical equations involves making sure that the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.
 
• It is essential to correctly use stoichiometric coefficients to achieve balance.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation-Reduction (Redox) Reactions:**
 
 
• The reaction between magnesium and oxygen is an example of a redox reaction.
 
• Magnesium is oxidized (loses electrons) and oxygen is reduced (gains electrons).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Magnesium Oxide:**
 
 
• Magnesium oxide (MgO) is a white, hygroscopic solid mineral.
 
• It is used in various applications, including as a refractory material and as an antacid.
 
 
 
• **Combustion Reactions:**
 
 
• The reaction between magnesium and oxygen is also classified as a combustion reaction.
 
• Combustion reactions typically involve a substance reacting with oxygen to produce heat and light.

questions.question: What is the major constraint in dry land farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low water availability**__.

• **Dryland farming **refers to agricultural practices in regions where rainfall is insufficient, typically less than **750 mm annually**, making water availability a critical constraint.
 
• The primary challenge in dryland farming is **low soil moisture** due to minimal rainfall, which limits crop growth and productivity.
 
• Crops grown in such areas are primarily **drought-resistant varieties**, such as millets, sorghum, and pulses, as they can survive with limited water.
 
• Dryland farming areas are also prone to **soil erosion**, which further reduces the land's capacity to retain water.
 
• Efficient water management techniques, such as rainwater harvesting and mulching, are critical to overcoming water scarcity in these regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dryland Farming:**

 
 
• It is a type of farming practiced in arid and semi-arid regions with low rainfall.
 
• Relies on moisture conservation techniques like **deep plowing**, contour farming, and minimal tillage to retain soil moisture.
 
• Crops such as pearl millet, chickpeas, and groundnuts are commonly grown in dryland farming systems.
 
 
 
• **Soil Moisture Management:**
 
 
• Techniques like **mulching** (covering soil with organic matter) help conserve moisture and prevent evaporation.
 
• Use of **micro-irrigation systems**, such as drip irrigation, ensures precise water delivery to crops.
 
 
 
• **Rainwater Harvesting:**
 
 
• Collecting and storing rainwater for agricultural use is a common practice in dryland regions.
 
• Helps supplement water availability during dry spells.
 
 
 
• **Drought-Resistant Crops:**
 
 
• These crops have evolved to survive with minimal water, making them ideal for dryland farming.
 
• Examples include **millets, sorghum, pigeon peas**, and certain oilseeds like sesame.

questions.question: What is the maximum percentage of reservation allowed for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) under the 103rd Amendment Act, 2019?

__
 
• The **103rd Amendment Act, 2019** introduced a provision for **reservation of 10%** for the **Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** of the general category in government jobs and educational institutions.
 
• This amendment added **Clause (6)** to **Article 15** and **Article 16** of the Indian Constitution to enable this provision.
 
• The reservation is aimed at providing social and economic justice to individuals who belong to the **general category** but face financial hardships.
 
• The criteria for EWS reservation include individuals whose family income is below **₹8 lakh per annum**, among other asset-related conditions.
 
• This is the first reservation provision in India based solely on **economic criteria**, rather than caste, tribe, or backward class categories.
 
• The cap of **10%** was decided to ensure that the overall reservation in India does not exceed the **50% ceiling** imposed by the Supreme Court in the **Indra Sawhney judgment (1992).**
 
• The amendment is widely regarded as a significant step toward addressing the needs of economically disadvantaged sections of society while balancing constitutional provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• Article 15(6) allows the state to make special provisions for the **advancement of Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)** in matters of education.
 
• This includes reservation in **educational institutions**, both aided and unaided, except for minority institutions.
 
 
 
• **Article 16(6)**__
 __
 
• Article 16(6) empowers the state to provide reservation to the **Economically Weaker Sections** in matters of **employment**.
 
• This ensures equal opportunity in public employment for individuals from economically weaker backgrounds.
 
 
 
• **Indra Sawhney Judgment**__
 
 
• The **Indra Sawhney case (1992)** established the **50% ceiling** for reservations in India to maintain the principle of equality.
 
• It also clarified the concept of **social and educational backwardness** as a basis for reservation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution explicitly declares laws violating Fundamental Rights as void?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 13** of the Indian Constitution explicitly declares that any law inconsistent with or violating Fundamental Rights shall be void.
 
• This Article ensures that Fundamental Rights, enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, remain supreme and protected from legislative infringement.
 
• It provides for judicial review, empowering courts to strike down laws that violate Fundamental Rights.
 
• Article 13 classifies laws into two categories: pre-Constitution laws (existing laws before January 26, 1950) and post-Constitution laws.
 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting Article 13 to ensure the protection of Fundamental Rights, making it a cornerstone of India's constitutional framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights** are basic rights guaranteed to all citizens under Part III of the Indian Constitution, ensuring equality, freedom, and protection against arbitrary actions of the state.
 
• **Judicial Review:** A process through which courts assess the validity of laws and executive actions to ensure compliance with the Constitution.
 
• **Doctrine of Eclipse:** Under Article 13, pre-Constitution laws conflicting with Fundamental Rights are not nullified but remain dormant, becoming enforceable if the conflict is removed later.
 
• **Doctrine of Severability:** If a part of a law violates Fundamental Rights, only the offending portion is declared invalid, and the rest remains operational.
 
• **Article 32:** Known as the "Right to Constitutional Remedies," it empowers citizens to approach the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena CANNOT be explained using the universal law of gravitation?

options.text: Motion of planets around the Sun
Motion of the moon around the earth

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Firing of a gun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The universal law of gravitation primarily deals with the gravitational attraction between masses.
 
• It explains the motion of celestial bodies like planets around the Sun and the moon around the Earth.
 
• Tides are influenced by the gravitational pull of the moon and the Sun on Earth's water bodies.
 
• Firing of a gun involves the forces of combustion, pressure, and projectile motion, not gravitational attraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Law of Gravitation**

 
 
• Formulated by Sir Isaac Newton, it states that every mass attracts every other mass in the universe with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• This law explains various phenomena including planetary orbits, free-fall, and the behavior of tides.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion**
 
 
• Describes the motion of an object thrown or projected into the air, subject to only the acceleration of gravity.
 
• Firing a gun results in projectile motion, where the bullet follows a curved trajectory due to gravity and initial velocity imparted by the gunpowder explosion.
 
 
 
• **Combustion in Firearms**
 
 
• When a gun is fired, the gunpowder combusts and rapidly converts into gas, creating high pressure.
 
• This pressure propels the bullet forward and out of the barrel.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Forces**
 
 
• Caused by the gravitational interaction between the Earth, Moon, and Sun.
 
• Tides result from the difference in gravitational pull on different parts of the Earth's surface.

questions.question: Heating of ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulphuric acid yields which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethene**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Heating ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulfuric acid results in the dehydration of ethanol.
 
• The dehydration process involves the removal of a water molecule from ethanol.
 
• This reaction produces ethene (C₂H₄), a colorless and flammable gas.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.
 
• Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst in this reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dehydration Reaction**

 
 
• A chemical reaction in which water is removed from a compound.
 
• Commonly occurs in the presence of a strong acid like sulfuric acid.
 
• Used to convert alcohols to alkenes.
 
 
 
• **Sulfuric Acid (H₂SO₄)**
 
 
• A strong mineral acid with strong dehydrating properties.
 
• Commonly used in the chemical industry as a catalyst.
 
• Can cause severe burns; hence, handle with care.
 
 
 
• **Ethene (C₂H₄)**
 
 
• Also known as ethylene.
 
• Used as a precursor in the production of polyethylene, a common plastic.
 
• Acts as a plant hormone involved in the ripening of fruits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ethene**
 
 
• Widely used in the manufacture of plastics and synthetic rubber.
 
• Employed in the production of ethanol and other chemicals.
 
• Utilized in agriculture to promote the ripening of fruits.

questions.question: Which of the following was used as the main electronic component in the fourth generation computers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The fourth generation of computers began in the early 1970s and is characterized by the use of **Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits (VLSI)** as the main electronic component.
 
• VLSI technology allowed the integration of thousands to millions of transistors on a single chip, significantly reducing the size and cost of computers while increasing performance.
 
• This generation marked the advent of **personal computers (PCs)**, making computing accessible to individuals and small businesses.
 
• Examples of fourth-generation computers include the IBM PC and Apple Macintosh, which revolutionized the computing industry.
 
• The use of VLSI circuits enabled the development of faster processors, larger memory capacities, and the ability to run complex software applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integrated Circuits (ICs):** The earlier third generation of computers used ICs, which integrated a few hundred transistors on a chip. VLSI advanced this by integrating millions of transistors.
 
• **Microprocessors:** The introduction of VLSI technology also led to the development of microprocessors, which are the central processing units of computers on a single chip. Examples include Intel 4004 and 8086.
 
• **Memory Technology:** The fourth generation saw advancements in memory devices such as RAM and ROM, which were also made possible by VLSI technology.
 
• **Software Development:** With the rise of personal computers, software development flourished, leading to the creation of operating systems like MS-DOS and graphical user interfaces (GUIs).
 
• **Impact:** VLSI circuits made computers more reliable, energy-efficient, and faster, paving the way for modern computing and the digital revolution.

questions.question: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor's regulations in Scheduled Areas can prohibit or restrict which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Land transfers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides special administrative provisions for the Scheduled Areas, primarily to protect the rights of tribal communities.
 
• The Governor of a state with Scheduled Areas is empowered to make regulations to prohibit or restrict the **transfer of land by or among members of Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• These regulations aim to prevent the exploitation of tribal land by non-tribal individuals or entities.
 
• The Governor can also regulate the allotment of land for agricultural purposes or settlement, ensuring the protection of tribal interests.
 
• The objective is to uphold tribal autonomy, safeguard their cultural identity, and prevent land alienation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Areas**

 
 
• Scheduled Areas are specified regions in India recognized for the protection of tribal communities under the Fifth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• These areas are identified based on the concentration of tribal populations and their socio-economic backwardness.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor**
 
 
• The Governor has legislative authority under the Fifth Schedule to make regulations for peace and good governance in Scheduled Areas.
 
• This includes the power to modify or nullify laws passed by the State Legislature in these areas.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Land Protection**
 
 
• The primary aim of restrictions on land transfers is to prevent the alienation of tribal land to non-tribals, which could lead to loss of livelihood and cultural erosion.
 
• Such measures also help in preserving the unique tribal identity and traditional rights of indigenous communities.
 
 
 
• **Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA)**
 
 
• PESA empowers Gram Sabhas in Scheduled Areas to safeguard and preserve the traditions, customs, and resources of tribal communities.
 
• It provides for self-governance and the management of natural resources by tribal groups.

questions.question: When iron filings are sprinkled around a magnet, they form a pattern. What does this pattern represent?

options.text: Both electric and magnetic field lines
Neither electric nor magnetic field lines

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic field lines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When iron filings are sprinkled around a magnet, they align themselves along the **magnetic field lines** of the magnet.
 
• These patterns visually represent the **magnetic field** and its direction.
 
• The iron filings experience a force in the presence of the magnetic field, causing them to move and align along the **field lines**.
 
• The density of the filings indicates the strength of the magnetic field; the closer the lines, the stronger the magnetic field in that region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic field**:

 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• It is produced by moving electric charges and intrinsic magnetic moments of elementary particles associated with a fundamental quantum property, their spin.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic field lines**:
 
 
• Magnetic field lines are a visual tool used to represent magnetic fields.
 
• They are imaginary lines that describe the direction of the magnetic force.
 
 
 
• **Ferromagnetic materials**:
 
 
• Materials like iron that can be magnetized are called ferromagnetic materials.
 
• These materials have high magnetic permeability and are strongly attracted by a magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetism**:
 
 
• Electromagnetism is the branch of physics involving the study of the electromagnetic force, a type of physical interaction that occurs between electrically charged particles.
 
• The electromagnetic force is one of the four fundamental interactions in nature.

questions.question: The ratio between the perimeter and the breadth of a rectangle is 5 ∶ 1. If the area of the rectangle is 216 sq. cm what is the length of the rectangle?

Ratio of Perimeter (P) to Breadth (B) is 5 : 1 ⇒ P = 5B

We know P = 2(L + B) ⇒ 2(L + B) = 5B ⇒ 2L = 3B ⇒ L : B = 3 : 2

Let Length = 3x and Breadth = 2x.

Area = 3x × 2x = 6x² = 216 ⇒ x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6

Length = 3x = 3 × 6 = 18 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 cm.**

questions.question: A solid right circular cone is 11.2 cm high and the radius of its base is 2.8 cm. If the cone is melted and recast into a sphere, then what will be the diameter of the sphere?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a cone is melted and recast into a sphere, their volumes are equal: (4/3)πR³ = (1/3)πr²h

⇒ 4 × R³ = 2.8² × 11.2

⇒ R³ = (2.8 × 2.8 × 11.2) ÷ 4 = 2.8 × 2.8 × 2.8

⇒ Radius of sphere (R) = 2.8 cm

⇒ Diameter of sphere = 2 × R = 2 × 2.8 = 5.6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5.6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of the cone (h) = 11.2 cm

Radius of the cone (r₁) = 2.8 cm

Let the radius of the sphere be r₂.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of cone = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × π × r₂³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7128069d41a45c97aeb86fb84ffff7a7a8a359e28703d0eae1802ac041486891.png] 

**Calculations:**

Since the solid right circular cone is melted and recast into a sphere, their volumes remain unchanged.

⇒ Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cone

⇒ (4/3) × π × r₂³ = (1/3) × π × r₁² × h

⇒ 4 × r₂³ = (2.8)² × 11.2

⇒ 4 × r₂³ = 2.8 × 2.8 × 11.2
